note: One of the famous openings of the Paradiso. Seen from Heaven, every earthly career looks like a bird beating its wings downward. Dante's Italian calls the reasoning behind them "defective syllogisms": bad logic, in the language of the schools.
Dante's word is aforismi, the Aphorisms of Hippocrates, the standard medical textbook. Law and medicine were the two paying professions.

context: Twelve lights have been dancing in a ring around Dante and Beatrice. Each has now come back to the place where it stood when their spokesman introduced them in Canto 10.
He named himself and the eleven other lights of his ring in Canto 10. He speaks for the rest of this canto.

note: The blessed see God directly, and in God they see everything, including Dante's thoughts. No one in Paradise needs to be asked a question aloud.
In Canto 10 Thomas called his Dominican order a flock on a road "where one grows fat, if he doesn't stray". The rest of this canto explains the remark.
Also from Canto 10: Thomas said of Solomon that no one ever rose to match his wisdom. Dante wonders how that can be true, given Adam and Christ. The answer waits until Canto 13.
The method of the medieval schools, and of Thomas's own books: a puzzle is solved by separating the senses in which a statement can be taken.

quote: the bride of Him who cried aloud
note: The Church, the bride of Christ. He "cried with a loud voice" as he died on the cross (Matthew 27), and his blood was the price of the marriage.

Francis of Assisi and Dominic, founders of the two great orders of friars at the start of the 13th century. One was to make the Church more faithful by his love, the other more sure of herself by his learning.
The Seraphim are the highest order of angels and burn with love; the Cherubim, next below, are filled with knowledge. Francis is the saint of love, Dominic the saint of wisdom.
Thomas, a Dominican, praises the founder of the Franciscans. In Canto 12 a Franciscan returns the courtesy and praises Dominic. On earth the two orders were often rivals.
A small river that runs below Assisi on the east. The other stream is the Chiascio, on the west. The riddling geography leads slowly to the town between them.
Ubaldo, bishop of Gubbio, who died in 1160. He had lived as a hermit on the hill near Gubbio where the Chiascio rises.
Monte Subasio. Assisi lies on its western slope.
The "Sun Gate" of Perugia, the gate that faces Monte Subasio, to the east. The mountain sends the city cold winds off its snow in winter and reflected heat in summer.
Two towns on the far side of the mountain. Their "heavy burden" is either the harsh climate in the mountain's shadow or, as many early commentators thought, the rule of Perugia.

quote: a sun rose upon the world
note: Francis. Bonaventure's life of the saint had already compared him to the angel of the Apocalypse who rises from the east (Revelation 7). The praise of a sun is spoken in the Heaven of the Sun.
For Dante the river Ganges marks the eastern edge of the inhabited world, where the sun comes up.
The hill town in Umbria where Francis was born. In Dante's Tuscan the name is Ascesi, which can also mean "I have risen". That is why the name "says too little".
The East, the place of sunrise. The Bible also uses "the Orient", the dawn from on high, as a name for Christ (Luke 1), whom Francis imitated more closely than anyone.
Francis's father, a wealthy cloth merchant, was furious when his son began giving away money and goods to the poor and to ruined churches.
Poverty, named at line 77. People shut the door on her as they would on death. Franciscan writers before Dante had already told the saint's life as a love story between Francis and Lady Poverty.

About 1207 his father brought him before the bishop of Assisi to make him give up his inheritance. Francis stripped off his clothes and handed them back to his father. Dante's Italian gives the words "in his father's presence" in Latin, like a legal record of a wedding.
Christ, who lived and died poor.
From the death of Christ to the conversion of Francis, nearly twelve centuries in which, Thomas says, no one loved poverty for its own sake.

A poor fisherman in Lucan's poem on the Roman civil war. When Caesar pounded on the door of his hut at night, he felt no fear, because he had nothing to lose. Even this famous praise of poverty won her no suitors.

quote: him who terrified the whole world

context: She stood at the foot of the cross while her son died on it.

quote: she climbed the cross with Christ
note: Christ died naked, owning nothing, not even a grave. Poverty alone stayed with him to the end, closer even than his mother.

context: Thomas has held back the name for more than thirty lines, telling the life as a riddle and a romance.

note: Bernard of Quintavalle, a rich man of Assisi and the first to join Francis. He gave all he had to the poor. Going barefoot was the mark of the new brothers.
Giles and Sylvester of Assisi were among the first followers. Sylvester was a priest, the first in the brotherhood.

context: Francis and his first companions set out for Rome to ask the pope's approval. The "humble cord" is the rope they wore as a belt.

note: A merchant's son, with no noble name, dressed like a beggar. He might have been ashamed to stand before the pope.

context: In 1209 or 1210 he approved the brothers' simple rule by word of mouth.

note: A seal makes a document official. The order receives three: the approval of one pope, the confirmation of the next, and finally the wounds of Christ on Francis's own body.

context: In 1223 he confirmed the final rule of the order in writing.

note: In 1219, during the Fifth Crusade, Francis crossed the battle lines in Egypt to preach to the Sultan, al-Kamil. The Sultan heard him courteously and sent him back unharmed.
In Dante's Italian these are the followers of Christ, not of Francis: he preached "Christ and the others who followed him", that is, Christ and the apostles.
La Verna, a mountain in the Casentino hills of Tuscany, between the upper valleys of the two rivers. Francis went there to fast and pray in 1224.
The stigmata: the five wounds of the crucified Christ, in hands, feet and side, which appeared on Francis's body at La Verna. He carried them until his death in 1226.
As he was dying, at the little church of the Porziuncola below Assisi, Francis asked to be laid naked on the bare ground. He left the world in Poverty's arms.
The Church, pictured as the boat of the fisherman Peter, the first pope. Thomas now turns from Francis to the other helmsman.

context: Thomas was a Dominican, so Dominic is the founding father of his own order. If Francis was so great, he argues, his partner must have been as great.
Thomas condemns his own order. The "new pastures" are usually taken to be honors, church offices and worldly studies, which draw the friars away from their founder's path.

note: The faithful friars are so few that a small piece of cloth would make hoods for all of them.
The Dominican order, a tree being hacked away as its members leave the founder's way.
The answer to the first puzzle. The sheep of Dominic's flock grow fat on spiritual food only if they keep to his road. Most, Thomas has just said, do not.
